comparators.basis: A correlation above 0.999 requires the reconstructed image morphology to remain nearly identical despite byte-level drift.
A two-percent relative L2 ceiling treats small numerical drift as acceptable while rejecting materially different images.
A two-percent relative L1 ceiling limits total absolute pixel drift.
A one-microarcsecond cross-run diameter tolerance is much narrower than the Paper VI 38–44 microarcsecond descriptive span.
A one-microarcsecond FWHM tolerance detects substantial changes while accommodating small numerical drift.
A 0.02 fractional-width tolerance is substantially smaller than the Paper VI upper range of approximately 0.5.
A 0.02 circularity-spread tolerance is smaller than the approximately 0.05–0.06 reconstructed-image distribution peak discussed in Paper VI.

limitations: These tolerances are engineering-derived by Vajra and have not been independently reviewed by the EHT Collaboration.
The comparison uses two GitHub-hosted workflow runs and the same OCI image, input data, pipeline, and scientific method.
Passing this contract establishes semantic cross-run stability, not universal bitwise determinism.
The contract does not identify whether drift originates from host CPU features, numerical libraries, thread scheduling, or undeclared pipeline randomness.
Passing supports the REC claim only and cannot promote the physical interpretation to S4.
